transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Helix - Head of ML), Derek Shaw (Helix - Platform Eng), Priya Rao (Helix - CTO), Samir Khan (Helix - ML Eng)
Shared artifacts: demo deck (link: /redwood/decks/model-playbook.pdf), bench spreadsheet (note: will share), console tour recording

00:00 Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Jordan, I'll run through the playbook and then Priya will walk the bench and routing demo. um, can everyone say hi?
00:08 Lena Ortiz: Hi this is Lena, yep thanks. we have a quick agenda?
00:12 Jordan Kim: Yep, agenda — 1) quick qualification, 2) model selection playbook in catalog, 3) live bench + routing demo in Console + Optimize, 4) Q&A and next steps.
00:22 Derek Shaw: Great. For context, our stack is mostly on GCP, some on-prem for regulated data; latency target is sub-150ms p95 for our search assistant, and cost needs to be competitive. we also have SOC 2 in progress.
00:36 Jordan Kim: Perfect, that's useful. Priya, want to take the catalog walkthrough?
00:40 Priya Desai: Yeah, thanks. so I'm in the Redwood Console -> Model Catalog. first thing we do is pick an objective "generation vs. chat vs. embed". for Helix, you said chat + rerank, so we'll filter for gen/chat and reranking-friendly models. note: the catalog has verified perf profiles — these are microbenchmarks run across sequences and hardware.
01:05 Miguel Alvarez: one quick note, sometimes the perf labels show up slightly different for quantized variants, like the q4 or int8 builds, those are flagged.
01:12 Lena Ortiz: that's helpful. how do you recommend we pick models for production? we care about quality + cost.
01:18 Priya Desai: Great question. our playbook is three steps: 1) shortlist by capability & safety tags, 2) run a lightweight bench with your prompts (we call this a scout bench), 3) pick a runtime family and config (hosted vs dedicated, quantization, batching). for Helix use-case, we'd start with 3 open models: a base Llama variant, an LLM-2 style open model, and a smaller llama2-ish for cheaper hits.
01:42 Samir Khan: when you say "scout bench" can you explain what you measure?
01:45 Priya Desai: latency distribution, token-per-second, perplexity/accuracy proxies on your prompt set, and hallucination frequency for a labelled subset. you get a compatibility matrix: quality vs runtime fit vs cost.
01:58 Jordan Kim: i'll add that Optimize gives quantization suggestions per workload — e.g., recommend q4_0 for latency-sensitive routes, or 8-bit if you can accept a slight quality delta.
02:10 Derek Shaw: What about KV cache behavior for long chats? we do conversational chains with 4k tokens typical.
02:15 Priya Desai: Right, KV cache performance is in the runtime profile. we show expected memory and latency impact per sequence length. small caveat: transcription sometimes shows this as "K V cash" in older exports, apologies.
02:28 Lena Ortiz: haha noted. show us the bench.
02:30 Priya Desai: switching to the Bench workspace — i'm uploading the scout prompts (these are placeholders, we'll run with Helix's later). starting the bench run now. you'll see a scatter of latency vs tokens; also a compatibility matrix that maps models to hardware families like A100, H100, and cost per 1k tokens.
03:02 [30s silence while bench runs, occasional typing]
03:32 Priya Desai: bench finished — quick take: Model A (open-llm-lite) has low cost but higher error rate on our instruction-heavy prompts; Model B (llm-2-ish) is good quality but higher cost on H100; Model C (compact) is cheap and meets latency but misses on some domain answers.
03:52 Lena Ortiz: that's pretty much what we'd expect. how do you handle routing and fallbacks? say Model B is default but if overloaded you fall back to Model C?
03:59 Priya Desai: Exactly. in Console -> Routing you define policies: priority routing by SLO, then cost. we show a policy editor: route to Model B for p50/p95 targets, fallback to Model C if queue latency > X or capacity shortfall. there is also automatic variant fallback to a quantized build if GPU is constrained.
04:24 Derek Shaw: Is that automatic? how deterministic is quality when you fallback to quantized builds? we need to audit for regressions.
04:31 Priya Desai: Great point. Redwood Optimize includes a regression checker: it runs the same labeled prompt set on both variants and flags quality drift. you can set a threshold for auto-fallback (e.g., only fallback if delta < 2% on your metric). we record traces and diffs so you have audit logs.
04:52 Priya Rao: On the compliance side — SSO, KMS, and audit logs — can you confirm options for our on-prem pieces?
04:59 Jordan Kim: Yes. Private deployments support customer-managed KMS and HSM integration, full audit logs forwarded to your SIEM, and SAML/SSO with SCIM. we'll share the security pack.
05:12 Samir Khan: will logs include raw prompt content? we have PII concerns.
05:17 Priya Desai: By default we redact PII in hosted, but for Private you control retention; we can set prompt redaction and token-level masking. we'll include that in the security doc.
05:27 Jordan Kim: quick detour — competitors are sometimes brought up: OpenAI for simplicity, Anthropic for safety-first models. our differentiation is the production playbook + routing and cost controls.
05:40 Lena Ortiz: can Redwood run a short pilot on Dedicated? we'd want to see end-to-end latencies with our traffic.
05:45 Jordan Kim: Absolutely. typical pilot is 2-week Dedicated pool with 2 GPUs and your prompt set; we'll run the bench and supply traces. Miguel will coordinate provisioning.
05:55 Miguel Alvarez: I'll follow up with a provisioning checklist and invoice/commit options.
06:00 [Timestamp jumps ahead: 06:00-15:00 omitted for brevity in export]
15:02 Priya Desai: Back to the Console — demoing the compatibility matrix. here you can click a cell and see the raw bench traces: token latency, GPU utilization, cache hits. there's also a small "explain" tab that suggests tuning like increasing batch size or enabling prefix cache for conversational patterns.
15:35 Derek Shaw: For our p95 <150ms goal, what do you realistically see on H100 vs A100?
15:40 Priya Desai: On H100 you can often get p95 ~110-140ms for shorter sequences; A100 might be 130-180ms depending on model. the bench shows distribution over your prompts. for long context we recommend smaller model variants with aggressive caching.
16:02 Samir Khan: any hard numbers you can share in the spreadsheet now?
16:05 Jordan Kim: We'll send the raw bench spreadsheet after the call — it includes per-prompt latency, tokens, and cost-per-call estimates.
16:13 Lena Ortiz: On the topic of model quality, how do you measure hallucinations? we need to ensure safety for finance domain.
16:20 Priya Desai: we run a labelled set where we mark hallucinations and use that as a regression metric. also, safety tags and red-teaming reports are in the catalog for curated models. for finance we recommend additional post-checks like rerankers or tool use with strong grounding.
16:40 Priya Rao: Are there standard integrations for our retriever + reranker stack?
16:45 Priya Desai: Yes, down to the SDK level — we have guide for integrating with your retrieval system and overlapping KV cache strategies. we also have examples in the quickstart repo.
16:58 Lena Ortiz: Any PTO around tokenization differences between models? we saw differences where same prompt tokenizes differently which affected cost.
17:04 Priya Desai: Yep, tokenizer differences are included in the bench — tokens-per-prompt is measured per model variant so costs are apples-to-apples.
17:15 Derek Shaw: A security question: will Dedicated in our VPC expose model logs to Redwood? we need data isolation.
17:21 Jordan Kim: For Dedicated and Private, you can choose whether logs are pushed to Redwood control plane; typically for high-reg customers we keep logs customer-side only and exchange aggregates. we'll get legal to map that out.
17:36 Samir Khan: ok cool. any notes on auto-scaling behavior under burst load?
17:42 Miguel Alvarez: autoscaling policies can be size-based or latency-based. we can configure cold-start limits and burst pools. there's also a "graceful degrade" policy: under capacity pressure, the router shifts percentage traffic to cheaper variants rather than dropping requests.
18:05 [Minor crosstalk — speaker overlap]
18:20 Lena Ortiz: recap for me — what will you share after this call?
18:24 Jordan Kim: we'll share: 1) bench spreadsheet + raw traces, 2) security pack (SAML/KMS/audit), 3) trial provisioning checklist, 4) short recording of this demo.
18:35 Lena Ortiz: perfect. and timeline? we aim to start a pilot by Oct 6.
18:39 Jordan Kim: That fits. we'll target provisioning before Oct 2 to give you time to test.
18:45 Priya Desai: final note — when you send us your 3 prompt sets and success criteria, we'll run a compatibility heatmap and surface the recommended runtime config and estimated monthly unit cost.
18:58 Derek Shaw: thanks all. one last: did someone mention regressions on quantized builds — want to see a quick example?
19:04 Priya Desai: sure — show quick diff: Model B vs Model B-q4: quality delta is 1.6% on our labelled metric, latency improves 28%. decision is yours if delta acceptable.
19:24 Lena Ortiz: ok great. we accept up to 2% drift for non-critical paths.
19:29 Jordan Kim: noted. any other questions?
19:33 Priya Rao: none immediate. we'll review the security docs and SSO details with our infra team.
19:38 Jordan Kim: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and set up the provisioning call.
19:44 Lena Ortiz: thanks, bye.
19:46 Meeting end.
